settings.title: Founded in 2014 by Hélène Rousseau after a decade in Paris couture houses.

settings.editor: Hélène wanted the craft of couture without its waste. Maison works with six family ateliers in Portugal and Italy, ordering in runs of 80 to 200 pieces so nothing ends in a landfill.
We publish the cost of every garment, pay our partners above the regional living wage and keep a repair workshop open for anything we have ever sold.

content.title: A field guide to natural dyes
content.excerpt: Madder, weld and walnut: how our dye house gets warm, living colour without synthetic fixers.
content.content:
Every terracotta in this collection started as a root. Natural dyes never give the same colour twice, and that is the point: each batch has its own depth, and it softens instead of fading.

The three plants we use most

  • Madder root for terracotta and rose.
  • Weld for straw yellows and, over indigo, olive.
  • Walnut hulls for sand, taupe and espresso.

How to care for naturally dyed linen

Wash cool with a pH-neutral detergent, turn the garment inside out and dry it in the shade. Expect the colour to mellow over the first few washes.

Synthetic colour sits on the fibre. Natural colour lives inside it.

Inês Moreira, head of dyeing

content.title: Lisbon in linen: a weekend wardrobe
content.excerpt: Seven pieces, one carry-on and three days of tiled streets, long lunches and evening light.
content.content:
Lisbon is a city of hills, so pack for walking. We spent a long weekend in Alfama with one carry-on and came back with more ideas than photos.

What we packed

  • Linen Suit Blazer and Wide-Leg Trousers — worn together and apart.
  • Silk Shirt for dinner at Prado.
  • Ribbed Wool Jumper for the miradouros after dark.
  • Suede Penny Loafers, broken in before the trip.

The trick is a palette that always works: ivory, sand and one warm accent. Everything goes with everything, so seven pieces become a dozen outfits.

content.title: The 30-piece wardrobe
content.excerpt: Why owning fewer clothes makes getting dressed easier, and the pieces we would keep.
content.content:
Most of us wear a fifth of what we own. A smaller wardrobe is not about rules; it is about keeping only the pieces you reach for first.

Start with what you already love

Pull out everything you wore last month. Look for repeats: the shape of trousers you trust, the colour you always pick. Those are your foundations.

Then buy slowly

Add one piece a season, in a fibre that will last. Natural fibres age well, can be repaired and do not shed microplastics in the wash.

Buy less, choose well, make it last.

Vivienne Westwood

settings.editor: Last updated 1 October 2026

Who we are

Maison runs this website. This policy explains what personal data we collect when you visit it, buy our clothing and accessories or contact us, and how we use it.

What we collect

  • Details you give us: name, email, phone, billing and delivery address when you order or get in touch.
  • Order details: what you bought, when and how you paid. Card numbers are handled by our payment provider and never stored by us.
  • Usage data: pages visited, device and browser, collected through cookies (see our Cookie Policy).

How we use it

  • To process orders, deliver what you bought and send receipts.
  • To answer questions and give support.
  • To send news or offers, only if you opted in. Every email has an unsubscribe link.
  • To keep the site secure and improve it.

Sharing

We share data only with services that help us run the business — payment, hosting, email and delivery providers — and only what they need. We never sell your data.

How long we keep it

Order records are kept for as long as tax law requires. Other data is deleted when it is no longer needed or when you ask us to.

Your rights

You can ask to see, correct, export or delete your data, or object to how we use it. Email care@maison-atelier.com and we will reply within 30 days.

Changes

If this policy changes we update the date at the top of the page.
Last updated 1 October 2026

About these terms

These terms apply when you use this website or buy our clothing and accessories from Maison. By placing an order you agree to them.

Orders and prices

Prices include the taxes shown at checkout. An order is confirmed when you receive our confirmation email. We may cancel an order if an item is unavailable or a price was shown in error, and refund you in full.

Payment

Payment is taken at checkout through our payment provider. Subscriptions renew automatically until you cancel them in your account.

Using the website

  • Do not misuse the site, try to break its security or copy its content for commercial use without permission.
  • Accounts are personal; keep your password safe.

Intellectual property

Text, images, logos and designs on this site belong to Maison or its licensors.

Liability

We do our best to keep the site accurate and available but cannot guarantee it is always error-free. Nothing in these terms limits rights you have by law as a consumer.

Contact

Questions about these terms: care@maison-atelier.com.
Last updated 1 October 2026

Our promise

If something is not right with your order, tell us and we will put it right.

Returns and refunds

  • Physical items: return within 30 days in original condition for a full refund.
  • Digital products and subscriptions: full refund within 14 days of purchase if you are not happy.
  • Services and bookings: cancel up to 7 days before the start date for a full refund.

How to ask for a refund

Email care@maison-atelier.com with your order number. Refunds go back to the original payment method within 5–10 working days.

Exceptions

Personalised items, used gift cards and services already delivered cannot be refunded unless they were faulty.
Last updated 1 October 2026

What cookies are

Cookies are small files saved by your browser. They help the site work and tell us how it is used.

Cookies we use

  • Essential: keep you signed in, remember your cart and keep checkout secure. These cannot be turned off.
  • Preferences: remember choices such as language or dark mode.
  • Analytics: count visits and see which pages are useful, only with your consent.
  • Marketing: measure campaigns, only with your consent.

Your choices

You can accept or reject non-essential cookies in the cookie banner and change your choice at any time. You can also delete cookies in your browser settings.

Contact

Questions about cookies: care@maison-atelier.com.
